verdict.summary: Assigning lastLockKeyboardId = smartMatchKeyboard() before the existing .default switch correctly moves the recovery anchor to the new schema and covers cached same-target layouts and non-lock full-Pinyin number/email fallback. The new head still requires device proof and remains Draft.

facts: 22:19:48.872 SchemaMessage selects luna_pinyin after the UI switched to default.
22:19:52.602 and 22:19:52.737 a new editor switches back to luna_pinyin_t9 while status remains luna_pinyin.
The pre-fix callback switches .default, but attachKeyboard updates lastLockKeyboardId only for locking keyboards, so full-Pinyin default cannot replace the old T9 anchor.

source_reasoning.cache_order: Rime.handleRimeMessage updates statusCached and schemaCached before messageFlow emission, so smartMatchKeyboard() in the downstream schema callback reads the new schema.
source_reasoning.t9_to_full: The anchor changes from luna_pinyin_t9 to the full schema match (default in the reproduced theme); the existing switch then attaches that layout. A later normal editor resolves to the new default rather than the old T9 lock.
source_reasoning.full_to_t9: The anchor changes to luna_pinyin_t9 before switching, and attachKeyboard preserves the same locking id.
source_reasoning.same_target_cached: The anchor assignment runs before switchKeyboard can take its cached target==current early return, avoiding the clear-to-empty variant failure.
source_reasoning.number_email: For full-Pinyin default(lock=false), a temporary number keyboard followed by .ascii can fall back to the new default anchor instead of an empty or stale T9 id.
source_reasoning.ordinary_same_schema_input: No schema callback occurs, so existing normal, FORCE_ASCII, number, tempAsciiMode, and per-keyboard ASCII state logic is unchanged.
source_reasoning.duplicate_schema_callback: Repeated callbacks for the same schema recompute the same schema default and the existing callback already switches .default, so the added assignment is idempotent at the intended state level.
source_reasoning.documentation: The added documentation accurately limits the reset to schema changes and describes the observed T9-to-full behavior.

residual_limits_and_tests: No APK built from b14a2f1e has yet supplied device proof; 1754 evidence is negative reproduction only.
Regression should cover T9 to full schema to a new normal editor, full to T9, schemes sharing a cached target, and full default to number to email/FORCE_ASCII to normal.

A theoretical burst of multiple schema callbacks can interleave with switchKeyboard main-executor posts and temporarily overwrite the anchor through a queued locking attach. This was not the reproduced single-switch path and is not treated as a blocker; the device sequence should still verify the final layout and schema together.
